title: Prior Authorization — Members Holding Several Authorizations
content:
**Clause.** A Prairie Ridge Health Plan member may hold any number of Prior Authorization authorizations across classes and services; each request is its own authorization.

**What this means.**

- There is no maximum number of authorizations per member: the plan sets no cap on how many a member holds at one time.
- A member may, for example, hold authorizations in different classes, or for different services within one class, side by side.
- Every request received is recorded as a separate authorization with its own authorization number, its own status and its own units.

**Basis Q&A.**

**Does opening a request in one class affect a member's authorizations in another class?** Not under this clause: each request is its own authorization, and the number a member already holds does not limit a further one.

**Hypothetical illustration.** A hypothetical member who holds an Advanced Imaging Authorization approval and an Outpatient Rehabilitation Therapy Authorization approval, and then has a Durable Medical Equipment Authorization request received, holds three separate authorizations, each with its own number.
